accepted_recoveries: Raise the search CPU request and limit to the benchmark's known-safe values after capacity checks.
Raise CPU capacity and tune the liveness timeout or failure threshold to the known-good fixture without disabling health detection.
forbidden_actions: Do not remove the liveness probe.
Do not set an unlimited CPU policy.
Do not lower benchmark traffic or weaken SLO measurement.
incident.injected_fault: The search container is capped at 100m CPU while its liveness probe has a one-second timeout, causing sustained throttling, probe timeouts, and restart cascades under load.
observable_signals: Container CPU throttling rises sharply during benchmark traffic.
Liveness probes time out and kubelet restarts otherwise functional search containers.
HTTP p95 latency and 5xx rate worsen in step with throttling and restarts.
preconditions: The load generator applies the same fixed profile before and after recovery.
Nodes and namespace quota have room for the known-safe CPU settings.
The search application has no independent dependency failure.
required_evidence: Capture CPU usage, CFS throttled periods, request, and limit.
Capture liveness probe settings and kubelet Unhealthy events.
Correlate throttling, probe failures, restarts, and request latency on one timeline.
Verify rollout stability and all SLO windows under the same load.

hypotheses.cause: The search-api container CPU request and limit are capped at 100m (0.1 CPU core) while its /healthz endpoint performs computational work (50ms CPU burn). Under incoming search traffic load, severe CFS CPU throttling causes the health check to exceed its 1-second timeout, triggering kubelet liveness probe failures and continuous restart loops.
supports: Deployment and Pod spec define resources.limits.cpu as 100m and resources.requests.cpu as 100m with annotation proofix.io/profile: 'injected-100m-cpu'.

SearchServer.java implements /healthz with burnCpuMicros(50_000), which requires at least 50ms of dedicated CPU time and easily starves when competing with 64-thread search request traffic under a 100m quota.
Kubelet Warning events show 'Liveness probe failed: Get \"http://10.42.0.139:8080/healthz\": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)'.
Pod status records restartCount: 4 and last termination exitCode: 143 (SIGTERM) directly following kubelet probe kill events.

hypotheses.cause: The Java SearchServer application is experiencing thread pool exhaustion, JVM stop-the-world garbage collection pauses, or an internal deadlock causing the HTTP server to hang on /healthz requests.
contradicts: SearchServer uses an unbound non-blocking / stateless architecture with simple atomic counters and independent thread execution without locking constructs.
JVM heap is configured to -Xms32m -Xmx128m within a 256Mi container memory limit, showing no OOMKilled events (termination exitCode was 143, not 137).
Pod starts up cleanly and passes initial startup and readiness probes until load-induced CPU throttling is applied.
supports: Liveness probe failed due to context deadline exceeded awaiting HTTP headers on port 8080.
Connection refused events were logged when probes attempted to connect while the container was restarting.

hypotheses.cause: Host node vm-4 is experiencing system-wide CPU/memory starvation or CNI/kubelet networking degradation preventing probe packets from reaching the container.
contradicts: Node vm-4 status reports 4 allocatable CPUs with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False, and KubeletReady=True.
Only search-api is experiencing failures; no node-level eviction, network partition, or kubelet crash events exist.
supports: Probe failures manifest as network dial timeouts and context deadline exceeded from the kubelet to 10.42.0.139:8080.

payload.rationale: The search-api deployment is configured with a 100m CPU limit and request. The application's /healthz endpoint executes a 50ms CPU burn. Under search traffic load, severe CFS CPU throttling prevents the probe from receiving sufficient CPU time, causing it to exceed the 1-second timeout. This leads to failed liveness probes and continuous SIGTERM restarts by kubelet. Raising the CPU request to 500m and CPU limit to 1000m provides sufficient compute capacity to handle concurrent search requests and complete health checks promptly without triggering restarts.
payload.rollback_trigger: Search-api pods fail to schedule due to resource constraints, crash on startup, or HTTP 5xx error rate exceeds 0.001 or p95 latency exceeds 200ms.

success_criteria.description: search-api pod reaches Ready status with 0 restart count increments, liveness probes pass consistently without timeouts, HTTP 5xx error rate remains < 0.001, and p95 latency remains < 200ms across 3 consecutive observation windows under benchmark load.

data.error: RuntimeError: kubectl command failed (1): The Deployment "search-api" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value

payload.rationale: The search-api container was throttled under benchmark traffic due to its 100m CPU limit, causing its CPU-burning /healthz endpoint to exceed the 1s timeout and trigger restart loops. The previous patch failed because JSON Merge Patch ('merge') replaces list fields entirely, causing Kubernetes to reject the container spec for missing required fields like 'image'. Switching to 'strategic' patch semantics merges the container resource limits into the existing container definition by matching on container name.
payload.rollback_trigger: Rollback if the deployment fails rollout, encounters CrashLoopBackOff, or fails to meet the SLO of p95 latency < 200ms and 5xx error rate < 0.001.

success_criteria.description: search-api deployment completes rollout with increased CPU resources (500m request / 1000m limit), liveness probes pass consistently without timing out, restarts stop, and p95 latency remains under 200ms with error rate under 0.001 across SLO measurement windows.
